decisions.question: Iter-2 scope shape: which verb set should iteration 2 ship?

options.label: Option A — minimum-viable (~7 verbs: contract read/write + peer_read_artifact + overseer alert only); defer checkpoint/anchor/task-gap to iter 3
Option B — full audit (~15 verbs across contract/checkpoint/peer/anchor/overseer/task-gap); one PR (Recommended)
Option C — staged iter 2 in two PRs: PR-2a (P0+P1 ~10 verbs: contract, peer, checkpoint, overseer, message send/poll), PR-2b (P2 ~4 verbs: anchor trio + task_mark_gap)
Option D — Option B plus also promote iter-1 best-effort phase_get_context fields (active_peers/reviewer_peers/hitl_pending) in the same PR
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Anchor approach: how should the MCP anchor verbs (init/update/get) be backed, given that orchestrator/routes/anchors.py REST endpoints exist but no `egg-orch anchor` CLI subcommand exists (despite rule docs referencing it)?

options.label: Wrap the REST endpoints directly with cli_command=None (same new-capability pattern iter 1 used for check_hitl_answers/get_context); acknowledge the drift test can't cover these
Add the missing `egg-orch anchor init/update/show` CLI subcommands to sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py first, then wrap those with the drift gate covered
Defer anchor verbs to a third iteration — too much scope for iter 2; keep the REST-only story as-is
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Checkpoint coverage: which egg-checkpoint subcommands should be exposed as MCP tools? (egg-checkpoint has 6: list, show, browse, context, cost, search)

options.label: All 6 subcommands (list, show, browse, context, cost, search)
Core 3: list, show, search — the verbs agents most likely need on the hot path
Core 3 + context — adds cross-agent context summaries, useful for reviewers/overseer
Core 3 + cost — adds cost accounting, useful if checkpoints become a budget signal for agents
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: task_mark_gap shape: how should tester→coder coverage-gap handoff be surfaced? (no CLI, no endpoint, no contract field exists today)

options.label: New orchestrator endpoint + new `task_gaps` field on the contract; add egg-contract mark-gap CLI; wrap as mcp__task__mark_gap with drift gate
Re-use existing `decisions` with a `type: task_gap` discriminator — no new endpoint, minimum schema churn
Add a dedicated `task_gaps` section on the contract (parallel to `tasks` and `decisions`) via a new endpoint; mcp__task__mark_gap wraps it; no CLI counterpart
No-CLI new capability (like brc_read_peer_artifact) — ship it MCP-only with cli_command=None; operators don't need it
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Namespace strategy: how should iter-2 verbs be grouped into mcp__<namespace>__* names?

options.label: Add new namespaces as needed — `checkpoint`, `overseer`, `anchor`, `peer` (up to 4 new namespaces); keeps each tool discoverable by semantic function

Stuff everything into the existing 5 namespaces — `sdlc` (show_contract, verify_criterion), `brc` (peer_read_artifact, send_message, poll_messages), `task` (add_commit, update_notes, mark_gap), plus overseer/checkpoint/anchor fit somewhere
Hybrid — add a new namespace only when the semantic group has >2 verbs (so: `checkpoint`, `anchor` likely yes; `overseer`/`peer` fold into existing namespaces)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Iter-1 phase_get_context field-promotion timing: active_peers / reviewer_peers / hitl_pending were marked best-effort in iter 1 (TD9); when should they become first-class required?

options.label: Include in this iter-2 PR — single rule-doc sweep, single review cycle
Separate follow-up PR after iter 2 — keep iter-2 scope focused on verb additions, not shape changes to existing tools
Leave best-effort indefinitely — the fields aren't hot-path enough to warrant hardening
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: verify_criterion REVIEWER-role gating: egg-contract verify-criterion requires REVIEWER role (contract_cli.py:1386). Where should the gating live for mcp__sdlc__verify_criterion?

options.label: Handler enforces — reads EGG_AGENT_ROLE; raises HandlerError if not a reviewer role; belt-and-suspenders with the gateway
Handler forwards — no role check in handler; gateway returns 403 which becomes GatewayError -> tool error block
Gateway already enforces — handler just forwards; document the role requirement on the tool description so agents self-select
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Peer-read-artifact source of truth: where should mcp__brc__read_peer_artifact read from?

options.label: Local .egg-state/brc-history/*.json files — simplest; no new endpoint; matches where reviewers dig today
New orchestrator endpoint backed by the same store — works across worktree boundaries; cleaner authz story
Hybrid — prefer the endpoint, fall back to file-reading; more robust but more code
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: EGG_MCP_TOOLS flag fate: #1946 flipped it default-on. What is iter-2's plan for the flag?

options.label: Remove the flag entirely during iter 2 — burn-in from iter 1 was sufficient; simplifies the code path
Keep the flag for iter-2 burn-in and remove in a third follow-up — same stepped rollout iter 1 used
Keep indefinitely as a kill-switch — never remove; always want the opt-out path
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Harness coverage: iter 1 decision-3 deferred EGG_HARNESS=egg parallel wiring. Should iter 2 address it?

options.label: Still defer — EGG_HARNESS=egg remains experimental; agents on that path keep shelling out
Add parallel wiring in this iter-2 PR — register iter-2 verbs on the egg harness too via shared/egg_harness_integration/
Track in a new follow-up issue — call out the gap but don't expand iter-2 scope
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Rule-doc drift gate: sandbox/agent-config/rules/*.md and sandbox/egg_lib/data/hitl_editing_rules.md carry `Prefer this over ...` notes that can drift silently. Should iter 2 add a CI guard?

options.label: Add a CI test symmetric with SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE drift: every `Prefer this over ...` entry in the rule docs must point at a registered tool, and every tool with a CLI counterpart must have a rule-doc entry (two-way)
One-way check only: every `Prefer this over ...` entry must point at a registered tool (catches stale removals, misses missing entries)
Skip — rely on manual review and the existing symmetric nudge drift test; rule docs can lag
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Tool-timeout contingencies: checkpoint_search and peer_read_artifact could exceed the 60s MCP timeout on large data. How should iter 2 handle this?

options.label: Paginate output by default — add `limit` / `cursor` params that keep any single call under 60s; agents page explicitly when needed
Start/poll/complete triplet for the two at-risk verbs — agent starts a job, polls for completion; heavier but handles arbitrary sizes
Accept the 60s ceiling — let agents retry or narrow filters on timeout; document the ceiling in tool descriptions
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: CLI-counterpart policy for new no-CLI capabilities: iter 1 allowed `cli_command=None` for new verbs (check_hitl_answers, get_context, list_blocking). What should iter 2's policy be?

options.label: Allow cli_command=None but require a docstring rationale explaining why no CLI exists; document the pattern in agent-tools.md
Require a shell CLI for every new verb even when human-useless — forces the drift gate to cover everything uniformly
Allow either; track the no-CLI tools in a separate list in agent-tools.md so reviewers can audit the exception set
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: mcp__brc__send_message / mcp__brc__poll_messages tool semantics: post-#1897 the legacy QUESTION message type was removed and reviewer clarifications moved to NACK `--reason`. Exposing raw `send`/`poll` risks re-opening off-protocol chatter and stepping on a planned REQUEST/REPLY subsystem. How should iter 2 scope these?

options.label: Ship both verbs; tool descriptions explicitly restrict use to HANDOFF/STATUS operator signals and steer clarifications back to NACK --reason
Ship poll_messages only (read-side) and defer send_message to land alongside the structured REQUEST/REPLY subsystem
Defer both verbs — agents already have mcp__brc__wait_for_event / wait_loop / send_heartbeat from iter 1 + #1897; directed send/poll wait for the REQUEST/REPLY subsystem
Ship both with narrow schemas that enumerate allowed message types only (HANDOFF, STATUS) — no freeform type strings accepted
Other (explain in reply)
